title.rendered: Sporting Lagos ship Akanji to Norway

content.rendered:
Sporting Lagos head coach, Jeffery Buter, has backed winger Seun Akanji to shine at Norwegian top-flight side Lillestrøm SK, following the completion of the 18-year-old’s permanent move to the Scandinavian club on a four-year deal.

Akanji was given an emotional send-off at his last training session with Sporting Lagos on Saturday, with Buter praising his development from an academy player to a key member of the club’s promotion-winning first team.

“It is actually interesting to see his progress. It is good to see an academy player come through the ranks, play for the first team, and help the team get promotion.

“It has been an honour to have you pass through this club. Personally, you are one of the most talented players I have coached. You have a very high ceiling if you keep your head low and you work hard,” Buter told the squad, before the players formed a guard of honour for the departing winger.

Akanji, visibly emotional, thanked his teammates and coaching staff as he bid farewell to the club.

“Thank you. I am going to miss you so much, you guys. I love you guys so much, and I want to say a big thank you to you all for what you have done for me so far. I love you guys,” he said.

The teenager arrives in Norway as one of Nigeria’s most exciting young talents, having played a pivotal role in Sporting Lagos’ promotion to the Nigeria Premier Football League, as well as the club’s Nigeria National League Super 4 title triumph.

Blessed with blistering pace, excellent dribbling ability and creativity in the final third, Akanji has long been regarded as one of the country’s brightest prospects, attracting interest from clubs beyond Nigeria before Lillestrøm secured his signature.

Although the transfer agreement had been concluded months ago, the deal has now been officially completed, paving the way for Akanji to begin the next chapter of his career in European football. The move also sees him reunite with fellow Nigerian talent, Kparobo Arierhi, at Lillestrøm, further strengthening the growing Nigerian presence at the Norwegian club.
